homeSummary: Christmas tree lighting and Advent news.
subtitle: The Sunday next before Advent
collect: Eternal Father, whose Son Jesus Christ ascended to the throne of heaven that he might rule over all things as Lord and King: keep the Church in the unity of the Spirit and in the bond of peace, and bring the whole created order to worship at his feet: who is alive and reigns with you, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, now and for ever. Amen.

notices.title: STOP PRESS: Snowman Concert postponed till January
notices.when: Christmas tree lighting: Sunday 29th November at 5pm (Refreshments served from 4.30pm).
paragraphs: Due to illness among several of the musicians, the Snowman Concert has had to be postponed till January, and the lighting of the Christmas Trees outside the Church will now take place on Sunday 29th November at 5pm (Refreshments served from 4.30pm).
There will be mulled wine provided free of charge by the Church (while stocks last) as a gift to the community, so do come along on the 29th and help celebrate the beginning of Advent.

notices.title: Open Doors
paragraphs: PLEASE NOTE: on Sunday 29th November at 10am in church, we will have John Barringer coming to speak on behalf of Open Doors a charity involved in helping persecuted Christians and we will be collecting donations for the charity’s work.

Every day, millions of Christians risk their lives to follow Jesus. In more than 70 countries, Open Doors supports them by supplying Bibles, providing emergency relief and helping persecuted believers stand strong for the long-term. In the UK and Ireland, Open Doors helps the church to pray, give and speak out for those who share our faith but not our freedom.

features.title: A message from the Food Bank……
paragraphs: “Within the next ten days we will be preparing bags of Christmas goodies for our clients. In order to get a good amount done in time, we therefore ask for the following this week:
Christmas Biscuits, Christmas-themed chocolate, Mince Pies, Christmas Pudding, Christmas Cake and Advent Calendars
We hope you will help us spread some joy this Christmas 🎄 Thank you for all you do for your neighbours in need.”

You can drop donations off in Church on Sunday morning, at the monthly Chapel Coffee morning (10am to 12noon), at The Stepping Stones pub, or at any time at any of the usual locations in Mickleham and Westhumble, details in the Parish Magazine.

features.title: SAFEGUARDING AUDIT SURVEY NOW OPEN
paragraphs: As part of the Church of England's independent safeguarding audit programme, the Diocese of Guildford and Guildford Cathedral are being audited by safeguarding specialists, INEQE. You can find out more about the audit on the diocesan website.
As part of this process, INEQE wants to hear directly from people across our parish communities about how we create environments where people feel safe, valued and respected.
The audit will help identify strengths in our safeguarding practice, as well as opportunities to learn, improve and build on what we do well.

There are separate survey links for different groups, including clergy and church staff, church members, those who attend parish activities, children and young people, and victims and survivors. The surveys are anonymous and confidential, and we encourage everyone to participate openly and honestly.
Survey links can be found here and will remain open until 1 January 2027.
If you have any questions about the audit, please contact the diocesan safeguarding team at ineqe@cofeguildford.org.uk
